hypothesis: Jerome called the grid updates the bottleneck of the whole method and improving grid BP 'the most valuable next step'. Every experiment runs at N_g = 401 on [-8, 8] (spacing 0.04), a setting chosen for convergence safety and checked only from above (E04, E11: 801 and 1601 change nothing). The exclusive-node time per sequence is 0.52 ms at N_g = 401 and 0.114 ms at 101 (E24x scaling, frozen): 4.6 times faster, which would move BP from 12-18 times slower than the transformer, the GRU and the U-Net (0.03-0.04 ms) to 3-4 times. The accuracy side was never measured, for the oracle or for the learned estimator.
design: Three parts. (a) ORACLE, deterministic, laptop: E32's refinement part, unmodified, with grids (21, 31, 41, 51, 61, 81, 101, 151, 201, 401, 801, 1601) on [-8, 8], reps 0-3, all six phi^4 cells; each grid's relative score error against the (1601, 8) reference. (b) LEARNED, cluster: experiments/e47_coarse_grid.py, E33's fit-and-score path with the BP grid coarsened: E33's own data, noised training views, validation and test bundles and REFERENCE posterior means (the true kernel on the registered 401-point grid), so a risk is the score error of the coarse-grid estimator against the fine-grid truth, discretisation included. Cells T0.3_h1_L32 (base) and T0.3_h0.25_L128 (the finest lattice, a Gaussian bond half as wide); M in (128, 2048); N_g in (51, 101, 201); arms em_pair_quartic and em_tilted_spline; seeds 0-7 (two shards of four: e47b-s0, s4); the comparators are E33's frozen fits at N_g = 401 on the same seeds (test-bundle hashes compared at read time). (c) TIME, cluster, exclusive node: E24's scaling part, unmodified, with grids (41, 51, 61, 81, 101, 151, 201, 401) at B = 512, L = 32, single thread, 9 repeats (e47-time).

predeclared_predictions.oracle: DESCRIPTIVE, no prediction: the oracle part was SCOUTED before this entry (64 chains, three levels, two cells): the relative score error of the true-kernel BP against the 1601 grid falls from 0.5-0.7 at N_g = 21 (t = 0.05) to 5e-4 at 51 and 1e-11 at 101 (super-exponential, the trapezoid rule on analytic integrands), so thresholds written now would be confirmed trivially. The full table is reported as it is.
predeclared_predictions.P1: Learned, base cell, M = 2048: at N_g = 101 and at N_g = 201 the seed-mean risk of each arm is within 1% of its N_g = 401 risk (ratio in [0.99, 1.01]).
predeclared_predictions.P2: Learned, base cell, M = 2048, N_g = 51: both arms within 3% of their N_g = 401 risk (ratio in [0.97, 1.03]).
predeclared_predictions.P3: Learned, finest lattice (T0.3_h0.25_L128), M = 2048: at N_g = 101 both arms within 1% and at N_g = 51 both within 10% of their N_g = 401 risk.
predeclared_predictions.P4: Learned, M = 128, both cells: at N_g = 101 both arms within 1% of their N_g = 401 risk.
predeclared_predictions.P5: EM fit time (site energy, base cell, M = 2048, median over the same seeds): at N_g = 101 at most one quarter, and at N_g = 51 at most one eighth, of E33's at N_g = 401 (not an exclusive-node measurement: both runs shared nodes, so indicative).
predeclared_predictions.P6: Time: BP at N_g = 51 takes at most 0.07 ms per sequence (B = 512, L = 32, exclusive, one thread), and at N_g = 101 within 20% of E24x's 0.114 ms (a replication check).
predeclared_predictions.P7: Time: the log-log slope of time per sequence against N_g over 41-401 is below 1.5 (elementwise work dominates; the N_g^2 law is a large-grid law).

predeclared_analysis: (a) refinement.csv: worst level and replicate per (cell, N_g); (b) kernels.csv risk-selected rows, per (cell, M, arm, N_g) the ratio of seed means to E33's N_g = 401 fits on the same seeds, test-bundle hashes compared, a failed fit counts against; wall per fit; (c) scaling.csv: ms per sequence by N_g; read by tools/make_extension_numbers.py.
provenance_note: Written after the oracle SCOUTING described under predeclared_predictions['oracle'] and after the E24x timings at N_g >= 101 were read; the learned-estimator and fit-time predictions (P1-P5) and the sub-101 timings (P6, P7) are not scouted. P1-P4 are tight (1% and 3%) because the oracle's discretisation error at 101 is 1e-11: a learned risk that moves by more than 1% would mean the kernel fit, not the quadrature, is what changes with the grid.
